€132.000—€132.000 EUR

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

allJobs.title: Accounts Payable & Financial Controller
allJobs.description:
Als Accounts Payable & Financial Controller ben je medeverantwoordelijk voor de juistheid, volledigheid en tijdigheid van onze financiële administratie — een van de belangrijkste pijlers voor het nemen van beslissingen binnen Crisp. Je combineert de dagelijkse sturing op de crediteurenadministratie met uitdagende controlewerkzaamheden, data-analyses en het automatiseren van onze processen met behulp van moderne tools en AI.

Wat je gaat doen

Je werkt elke dag met een gezellig team vol gedreven mensen. We hebben ervaring in business control, accounting, corporate finance, data analytics, fiscaal recht en auditing. Crisp groeit snel, en de verantwoordelijkheden van ons team dus ook. Zo is geen dag hetzelfde en blijven we onszelf continu ontwikkelen. We sparren veel en staan open voor elkaars mening.

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het verwerken en controleren van inkomende facturen en declaraties. Je staat leveranciers te woord, beheert de mailstroom en zet betalingen klaar.

  • Je stuurt een team van werkstudenten en stagiaires aan en zorgt er samen met hen voor dat alle facturen tijdig en correct worden verwerkt.

  • Je ondersteunt bij de maandafsluiting, controleert grootboekrekeningen en helpt mee met ad-hoc analyses en periodieke rapportages.

  • Je denkt actief mee over het slim inrichten van financiële workflows. Je verkent en implementeert mogelijkheden voor procesautomatisering, slimme datakoppelingen en AI-oplossingen (zoals OCR-herkenning en geautomatiseerde factuurverwerking).

  • Je rapporteert aan de Lead Financial Controller, die je ondersteunt in je dagelijkse werkzaamheden en je helpt om door te groeien in je rol.

Dit ben jij

Als ideale kandidaat heb je al een basis aan kennis en ervaring en wil je blijven leren in een vakgebied dat continu verandert en digitaliseert. Je herkent jezelf in het volgende profiel:

  • Je beschikt over een afgeronde hbo- of universitaire opleiding (bijvoorbeeld Finance, Bedrijfseconomie of Accountancy).

  • Je hebt 0-3 jaar relevante werkervaring in een financiële of control-functie.

  • Je hebt ervaring met de crediteurenadministratie en het verwerken en controleren van facturen.

  • Kennis van accountingsoftware (zoals Exact) is een pré.

  • Je bent handig met data en hebt een sterke affiniteit met automatisering en nieuwe technologieën (zoals AI-tools, data-integraties en procesoptimalisatie).

  • Je schrijft en spreekt vloeiend Nederlands en Engels.

  • Je bent integer, nauwkeurig en risicobewust. Je begrijpt dat een strakke administratie de basis vormt voor goede besluitvorming.

  • Je denkt in kansen en mogelijkheden: je ziet direct waar processen sneller, slimmer of foutlozer kunnen en schroomt niet om dit op te pakken.

Wat wij bieden

  • Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op het Europese voedselsysteem.

  • 27 vakantiedagen om bij te komen en op te laden.

  • Een extra vrije dag per jaar om je in te zetten voor vrijwilligerswerk en iets goeds te doen.

  • Aandacht voor je mentale gezondheid met online begeleiding van erkende psychologen via OpenUp.

  • Voor straks een perfect pensioen via BPFL.

  • Elke maand food for thought, met workshops en talks via de Crisp University.

  • Regelmatig tastings of workshops op kantoor of bij een van onze leveranciers, om te zien hoe onze lekkerste producten worden gemaakt – en natuurlijk ook te proeven.

  • Dagelijks een uitgebreide, georganiseerde lunch op kantoor.

  • Enthousiaste, slimme collega’s en tijd om elkaar te leren kennen tijdens sport, events en proeverijen.

  • En... fikse korting op je Crisp boodschappen, omdat je thuis natuurlijk ook goed wilt eten.

Onze selectieprocedure

Solliciteer via onderstaande button. Hoe meer je kunt delen over jezelf en de reden dat je solliciteert, hoe beter.

Bij Crisp streven we naar een inclusieve en diverse werkomgeving waarin iedereen welkom is, ongeacht hun achtergrond, geslacht, leeftijd, etniciteit, seksuele geaardheid, religie of beperking. Wij moedigen sollicitanten met diverse perspectieven en achtergronden aan om te solliciteren en geloven in gelijke kansen voor iedereen. We waarderen de unieke bijdragen die elke medewerker kan leveren en zijn vastbesloten om een inclusieve werkplek te creëren waarin iedereen wordt gerespecteerd en gewaardeerd.

allJobs.title: Audit Methodology Lead
allJobs.description:
We build AI agents that perform audit procedures for audit firms. We need an experienced auditor to decide what correct output from those agents looks like, and whether our agents meet that bar.

You'll join one of our product groups as its audit expert. You'll write the criteria and reference cases our agents are tested against, review agent output the way you'd review a file, and tell the team plainly when something isn't ready for a live engagement. You'll use AI to create realistic test material, and you'll review all of it yourself.

About DataSnipper

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust.

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

And we build at scale. More than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on DataSnipper, including Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. In 2025 alone, the DataSnipper platform delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to is customers. Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way.

 

What you'll own

  • Define the correct answer, and the reasoning behind it, for the procedures our agents perform

  • Interpret ISAs and NV COS (IFRS for reporting matters; US GAAS and PCAOB where relevant) into requirements engineers can build against

  • Create realistic audit cases with AI tools, including documents, workpapers, exceptions and judgement calls, and review every one

  • Review agent output against those cases, and find misapplied standards, weak reasoning and conclusions that wouldn't pass partner review

  • Turn recurring errors into findings product and engineering can fix

  • Give a clear, evidenced view on whether a capability is ready for live engagements

  • Review methodology content from partners and our own teams, with versioning, approval and documented changes

  • Track changes in standards and inspection findings, and explain what they mean for the product

  • Teach product and engineering how audit work is actually done, including how firms differ

  • Work with customers and content partners when the work requires it

What you'll bring

  • A professional qualification: RA, AA, CPA, CA, ACA, ACCA or equivalent

  • Experience as an Audit Manager: setting the approach, reviewing others' work, clearing review notes and defending conclusions

  • Recent experience across several clients and industries

Mission of this role

Thousands of rental companies run their business on Rentman, and many of them depend on it talking smoothly to the rest of their stack: accounting packages, webshops, calendars, and our public API. When an integration breaks, invoices don’t sync, bookings go missing, and customers notice fast.

As Senior QA Specialist for the Integrations team, you make sure every release reaches those customers without regressions.   • Hands-on experience with AWS for production workloads.

  • Solid understanding of web security best practices (OWASP, secure storage, encryption in transit/at rest, secrets management).

  • Excellent async communication, code ownership, and ability to work with a small, senior-led team.

  • Comfort working from a clear product brief and also proposing improvements proactively.

  • Familiarity with logging, monitoring, and observability tools.

Take-home assignment (Step 1 of the process)

Please complete a take-home assignment. You are allowed to use LLMs to write code. To ensure that your work will not be used at Fluence, we’ve made it unrelated to healthcare:

Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows

A simple app where neighbors list tools they are willing to lend, request to borrow from each other, and receive automated notifications and reminders handled by n8n.

Stack

  • Next.js (App Router)

  • Clerk for authentication

  • Convex for data + backend logic

  • n8n (self-hosted via Docker or n8n Cloud) for workflow automation

  • TypeScript

Requirements

Public page

  • The fictional company name is LendLoop.

  • Short tagline, e.g. “Borrow what you need. Lend what you don’t.”

  • Show:

  • A read-only list of available tools (name and category only, no owner details), pulled from Convex.

  • A “Sign in to lend or borrow” button wired to Clerk.

Authenticated experience

  • Only signed-in users can:

  • List a tool with:

  • name

  • category (power tools, garden, kitchen, camping, etc.)

  • condition

  • short description

  • Request to borrow a tool for a date range.

  • Approve or decline requests on their own tools.

  • Mark a loan as returned.

  • Show:

  • All tools with availability status, filterable by category.

  • “My listings”, “My requests”, and “Incoming requests” views.

  • Nice, minimal layout.

Roles & rules

  • Have two roles:

  • admin:

    • Can remove any listing, view all loans, and mark a lender as “Trusted Lender”.

  • user:

    • Can create, edit, and delete only their own listings, and act only on requests involving their own tools or their own borrowing.

  • Implement the above role-based access control with best practices, enforced in Convex functions, not only in the UI.

Automation with n8n

  • Build at least two n8n workflows:

  • Request notification: when a borrow request is created or changes status, Convex calls an n8n Webhook. The workflow notifies the relevant user (email, Slack, Discord, or a logged mock notification is fine) using only the fields it needs.

  • Overdue reminders: a scheduled workflow runs daily, fetches overdue loans from a Convex HTTP endpoint, sends a reminder to each borrower, and writes the reminder status back to Convex.

  • Secure the integration in both directions:

  • Sign webhook payloads (e.g. HMAC with a shared secret) and verify signatures on the receiving side.

  • Keep secrets in environment variables and n8n credentials, never in code or exported workflow JSON.

  • Make write-backs idempotent so retries do not create duplicate records or reminders.

  • Handle failures with retries and an error workflow (or equivalent) so failed runs are visible and never fail silently.

  • (Bonus) Show recent automation activity on each loan in the app, e.g. “Reminder sent 2 days ago”.

Deliverables

  • A GitHub repository with the app source code.

  • Exported n8n workflow JSON files in the repository.

  • A README covering local setup (including n8n, e.g. a docker-compose file), environment variables, architecture, and your security and data-minimization decisions.

  • A short note on what you would change to run this in production.

We evaluate:

  • Code structure and clarity

  • Security-minded thinking

  • UX and practicality

  • Integration design, reliability, and error handling (n8n)

  • Documentation and reasoning

Interview Process

  1. Take-home assignment submission (as described above).

  2. Technical & product interview (walkthrough of your solution, architecture, security mindset, collaboration style).

  3. 6-month contract offer for the right candidate, with strong potential for renewal as a recurring contract based on performance and ownership.

How to apply

Email your portfolio, GitHub repository, and as an optional bonus, 1-2 other relevant projects to techjobs@fluencetraining.com, along with a short note on a security/privacy consideration you implemented (or would implement) in a healthcare or similar context.

How it works

 

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

 

Requirements

 

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering
  • Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
  • Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
  • Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
  • Regular use of an AI coding tool
  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
  • At least 10 hours a week, starting now
  • A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

 

Nice to have

 

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
  • Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

 

Terms

 

  • US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
  • The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
  • Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

 

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

allJobs.description:
About Mitre Media

Mitre Media is redefining FinTech with AI-driven tools that empower millions of investors. Our portfolio, including Dividend.com and MutualFunds.com, leverages LLMs to deliver novel data insights and visually rich user experiences. For over a decade, we’ve served individual investors, financial advisors, and top asset managers like BlackRock and Vanguard through our premium data, tools, and advertising solutions. Join our lean, entrepreneurial team to shape the future of AI-powered investing from your location ±3 hours from Eastern Time.

Our users are deeply engaged, spending over 5 minutes per visit with a bounce rate below 10%, researching investments across hundreds of different categories. With 40 million brokerage accounts in the U.S., we take pride in building tools that make a real impact, fostering a culture of trust, innovation, and dynamism. If you’re passionate about financial technology and AI, we’d love to connect!

About the Role

As a Full-Stack Rails Tech Lead, you’ll architect and implement LLM-powered web applications within our microservices-based Rails 8 platform. Reporting directly to our CTO, you’ll collaborate with a small, high-impact team to deliver user experiences across Dividend.com, MutualFunds.com and other brands within our portfolio. This role combines expert Ruby on Rails skills with AI integration expertise, requiring you to leverage LLMs in your development workflow, state management and user interactions.

You’ll work in a remote-first hybrid environment, which encourages in person collaboration, using ShapeUp to manage projects that trade-off on-time delivery for de-scoped outcomes. As a technical leader, you'll have a seat at the table shaping system architecture, implementing core features all while embracing an entrepreneurial mindset and a “get things done” mentality.

Responsibilities

  • Integrate LLMs into our microservices architecture for state management and real-time user experiences.

  • Enhance front-end experiences with Hotwire, StimulusJS, or React, ensuring seamless AI-driven interactions.

  • Optimize LLM inference for low latency and cost, using caching and asynchronous processing.

Required Technical Skills

Back-End

  • Ruby (5+ years, expert-level)

  • Ruby on Rails (Rails 6-8 preferred)

  • PostgreSQL (or MySQL)

  • Elasticsearch

  • Redis

  • Docker

Front-End

  • StimulusJS or JavaScript ES6

  • Tailwind CSS

  • HTML

  • HTTP

AI Integration

Nice-to-Have Technical Skills

  • Kubernetes for microservices orchestration

  • Attention to detail, ensuring clean, maintainable code

Why Join Us?

  • Impactful Work: Build AI-powered tools that help millions of investors make informed decisions from data-driven insights.

  • Cutting-Edge Tech: Work with Rails 8, LLMs, and modern tools like Hotwire, Databricks, and xAI’s API in a microservices architecture.

Come build something with us! Role Summary The Client Accounting Division Manager runs their division as a self-contained business unit within Burkland. The manager also owns key client relationships and serves as the first-line escalation point for client issues, with a defined handoff path for anything beyond their resolution. This job description outlines the core of the role, but it isn't meant to cover everything you'll do. As Burkland grows, your responsibilities may shift and new projects, tasks, or priorities may be added along the way. We hope you'll see that as a chance to stretch, learn, and broaden your contributions. Essential Duties & Responsibilities Division Performance and KPI Accountability Own the business unit's P&L, including revenue, margin, and utilization targets. Monitor team capacity and engagement to support retention and prevent burnout. Apply company policies consistently, manage time-off and leave requests, and bring performance concerns, employee relations matters, and escalations to the Director and People Team for guidance and resolution. Plan staffing against current and forecasted client demand and build the business case for new headcount. Lead hiring for the division through interviewing and selection, and onboard new team members so they reach full productivity within expected timelines. Inventory Accounting and Technical Oversight Oversee inventory valuation, reconciliation, and physical and cycle count processes across the divisionâs client portfolio, making sure variances are investigated and resolved quickly. Set standards for costing methods (FIFO, LIFO, weighted average) and ensure the team applies them correctly by client and industry. Ensure the team delivers accurate GAAP financial statements, inventory reporting, and COGS and gross margin analysis tailored to each clientâs business model. Coach the team to help clients reduce shrinkage, obsolescence, overstocking, and stockouts, and to improve working capital through metrics like inventory turnover and days on hand. Strong understanding of supply chain methods such as contract manufacturing and 3PL operations Client Relationships and Service Quality Act as an escalation point for client relationship issues. Oversee quality control to ensure deliverables meet firm standards. Shift the team's work from solely report delivery toward proactive advisory. Growth and Operations Own growth of the division's book of business through business development efforts to expand existing client relationships and identify service-expansion opportunities Maintain accurate, current portfolio information in Knownwell Drive full adoption of firm tools, systems, and processes, including AI-enabled workflows Group and Company Success A One Burkland mindset: Our clients are best served when teams work together, not in silos. Partner closely with Tax, CFO, HR, and other service lines to create consistency, share knowledge, and deliver a seamless client experience across Burkland. Comfort with an increasing pace of change : Today's pace is the slowest we will experience going forward, not a finish line before things settle. As AI and related tools evolve, our processes evolve with them. This allows for more chances to learn, grow, and shape how the work gets done. This is about changing how the work gets done, not reducing the need for skilled people to do it. A constructive attitude: Attitude is contagious in both directions, across the team and with clients. Approach change with curiosity and enthusiasm. Help to set that tone for others rather than defaulting to resistance. Delivery and proactive advisory: Build real understanding of where each client's business is headed and advise ahead of it. Clients need the why behind their numbers, not just the numbers. Leading Change â Champions of change, including AI-driven efficiency, leading by example in the consistent adoption of firm tools, systems and processes and reinforcing them across the team. allJobs.description: Software Engineer, Infrastructure Hybrid in Palo Alto (Mon / Wed / Thurs) Â· $185Kâ$215K base + meaningful early-stage equity + full benefits Â About Sodalis Specialty pharmacy is where the most complex and expensive drugs reach the most in-need patients, and it still runs on faxes, phone tag, and manual data entry. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait. Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist. We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx). Â The Opportunity Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own. We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live. We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range. You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture. What you'll do Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between. Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy. Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site. Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range. Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture. What we're looking for 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering. You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services. You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded. You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them. You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity. You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required. How we work We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. It's intense, and it isn't for everyone. We want people who want to build something that matters, alongside others who care as much as they do. If that's you, we should talk. As Partnership Operations Manager, you will own that path for our regional partnership leads so they can focus on finding and signing partners. This is a new function, so you will set the standards and tooling yourself and make them repeatable across regions. What You Will Do Deal support: Prepare proposals and agreements from approved templates and keep a clean record of every partnerâs rates, volumes, and term dates. Onboarding: Set partners up on the platform, issue devices and accounts, and train their teams on capture standards so they reach full output quickly. allJobs.title: Graduate Transport Planner
allJobs.description:
At Curtins, we're an employee-owned engineering consultancy driven by a simple ambition: to create a better built environment for everyone.

For over 65 years, we've delivered practical, innovative and sustainable solutions that make a positive impact on communities across the UK and Ireland. From major regeneration schemes and commercial developments to education, healthcare and residential projects, our work helps shape the places where people live, learn, work and thrive.

As a Graduate Transport Planner, you'll work alongside experienced planners, engineers and consultants, contributing to a wide range of projects while developing the technical and professional skills you need to build your career.

Whether you're interested in transport assessments, active travel & sustainable mobility, highways or public transport, we'll give you the experience, guidance and support to find the areas that interest you most and develop your expertise in development planning.

What you'll be doing

You will support the planning and development process, helping clients bring projects forward from initial concept through to planning approval.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Assisting with the preparation of Transport Assessments and Transport Statements.

  • Supporting the production of Travel Plans and technical planning reports.

  • Analysing traffic, transport and movement data.

  • Assisting with junction assessments and development impact studies.

  • Supporting planning applications for residential, commercial and mixed-use developments.

  • Working alongside planners, civil engineers and other specialists to deliver integrated solutions.

  • Attending client meetings, project discussions and stakeholder consultations.

  • Taking part in wider Curtins activities including STEM outreach, charity initiatives and community projects.

What kind of projects will I get to work on?

You'll be involved in projects across a wide range of sectors, including:

  • Residential developments.

  • Urban regeneration schemes.

  • Commercial and industrial projects.

  • Education and healthcare developments.

  • Mixed-use masterplans.

  • Strategic land and development opportunities.

You'll help assess how developments interact with the transport network and support clients through the planning process, helping turn ideas into deliverable projects.

How will Curtins support my development?

Our goal is simple: to help you become the best engineer you can be.

Through the Curtins Graduate Academy, you'll follow a structured development programme designed to accelerate both your technical and professional growth.

You'll benefit from:

  • A structured graduate development programme.

  • Dedicated mentoring and coaching.

  • Regular technical and professional skills training.

  • Support towards professional registration and Chartership.

  • Exposure to a wide range of projects, clients and sectors.

  • Opportunities to build your network across the business.

You'll be supported by experienced professionals who are genuinely invested in your success and development.

What we're looking for

We're looking for graduates who are curious, analytical and interested in how development projects are planned and delivered.

You'll ideally be studying towards or have recently completed a degree in:

  • Transport Planning

  • Geography

  • Urban Planning

  • Civil Engineering

  • Town Planning

  • Geography or a related discipline

It would also be advantageous to hold an MSc in Transport Planning, Transport Engineering, Urban Planning, or Development Planning.

Most importantly, we're looking for people who share our values:

Integrity - Doing the right thing.

Being Human - Supporting and respecting others.

Curiosity - Asking questions and seeking better solutions.

Impact - Making a meaningful difference through our work.

Why join Curtins?

As an employee-owned business, every person at Curtins contributes to and benefits from our success.

Alongside exciting projects and a supportive culture, you'll enjoy:

  • Industry-leading benefits package.

  • Award-winning training and development programmes.

  • Employee ownership benefits.

  • Opportunities to get involved in STEM, charity and community initiatives.

  • Access to our unique Employee Extras, including our 5-star holiday lodges.

Most importantly, you'll be joining a business where your ideas matter, your development is supported and your contribution makes a real difference.

Build your future with Curtins.

Should you wish to discuss any adjustments to the application process or provide us with feedback please contact hr@curtins.com we would be happy to discuss ways we can make the process more suitable to your needs.

We value diversity and respect all differences in people. We invite enthusiastic individuals who share in our values of teamwork, client focus, integrity, and quality to apply to join us.

Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves. They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world. Responsibilities & Mandates ï¸ Systems that hold up We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. All in on agentic development The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. allJobs.title: Technical Customer Support
allJobs.description: QuickMail is a cold email and LinkedIn outreach platform for markets you can't afford to burn. Our customers can't easily replace leads that land in spam, which is why deliverability matters more to us than anything else. We have been running since 2014, and we pioneered deliverability technology such as Inbox rotationâ¢ and deliverability AIâ¢. The Role We are hiring a technical customer support person with an owner's mentality. You will own support for QuickMail and Mailflow, our deliverability add-on. There is no first or second line. You are the first and last person our customers talk to. Customers count on you to solve their problems and find the real cause when something breaks. You work closely with engineering, and you tell the founder what we need to know to make the product better: where the friction is and where the opportunities are. The role covers the help desk, system health checks, testing new releases before they ship, and leading the weekly team meeting. It takes excellent communication, solid technical understanding and sharp critical thinking. This is not a script-reading job. Most tickets involve deliverability, DNS records, LinkedIn automation or campaign setup. You dig into customer accounts in our Support Dashboard, reproduce the issue, then decide what to do and how to explain it to the customer. We are a remote team spread across time zones. Most routine tasks have a written guide with a checklist, so you know what done looks like. You are expected to refine and improve those processes. When something new comes up, you work out the most efficient way to handle it. If you want a lot of autonomy across many areas, real responsibility and a fast-paced environment, this role is for you. What Work Looks Like You own two things: customers get unstuck fast, and the product stays reliable. Every day Set the day's support priorities and work the Help Scout queue for QuickMail and Mailflow. Triage, resolve, and dig deeper when a ticket needs it. Check the support dashboard: job queue, event-stream latency, blacklist status, newly purchased domains. If something is off, investigate, diagnose, and drive it to resolution. Review fraud alerts and disable accounts that are scams or abusing the platform. Delighting customers Comfortable jumping on calls with customers, building rapport fast, and setting them up for success. Update the changelog and help articles based on what shipped and what customers asked. Share customer feedback with the team, ask happy customers for reviews and case studies, and watch NPS for testimonial candidates. Making support smarter with AI Improve the AI support agent. Review its answers, fix the docs it drew from when it is wrong, and contact the customer when its reply was off. Write and maintain automated tests, built with AI, that try to break staging before customers do. Use the MCP connections we have in place (Helpscout, GitHub, Postmark, and others) to get an accurate picture of support and find the next thing worth improving. Keeping the product solid Gatekeep releases. New fixes and features land on staging every week. Test them, confirm when staging is ready to ship, and think through how existing and new users will be affected. Report bugs as GitHub issues with everything the developer needs: steps to reproduce, screenshots or a Loom, and any GraphQL or console errors. Captain red alerts. When a core feature breaks (emails not sending, login down), confirm it, alert the team on Slack or Telegram, update the status page every 30 minutes, keep affected customers informed, and drive the fix. Then run the retrospective so it does not happen twice. Running the week Lead the weekly team meeting in MonsterOps: issues written up, to-dos done, numbers updated. Keep rock status and KPIs current in MonsterOps. Tools you'll use: Helpscout, our Support Dashboard, Sidekiq, GitHub, Slack, Telegram, MonsterOps, Outline, MxToolbox, Postmark, Bento, TidyCal, Fathom, Visual Code and Claude. Who You Are You build rapport fast. You are warm, positive, and relatable in writing and on calls. You are a good communicator. Externally, you can show warmth, empathy and care. Internally, you are able to communicate clearly and concisely about important things. You can operate with minimal instructions. You understand a short brief without every detail spelled out. You can prioritize well (especially when you have a lot on your plate), and get things done without hand-holding. You are comfortable on video. You are natural on live calls with Zoom and Meet, and on recorded video through tools like Loom. Your teammates can always count on you. You say what you'll do and you do what you said. You act with a constant sense of urgency. You can execute fast and find new ways to improve your productivity. You are resourceful. You use all the tools at your disposal to get great results. You have a low ego. You don't take offense easily and you handle disagreement as a discussion, not a personal attack. Growth mindset. You are positive about new workflow/process/product/tool changes. You love giving and receiving positive and negative feedback without getting defensive. Hours that overlap with East coast US and UK, where most of our customers are. A Plus If You Have Experience with customer facing work, or if you don't have it, tell us why you are perfect for this role. Working knowledge of deliverability and LinkedIn outreach. Warmup, DNS, inbox rotation, DKIM, SPF, Outlook and Gmail technical setup. We can teach this, but a head start helps. Comfort with agency setups. Workspaces, guest seats, inbox purchases and what happens when an agency loses a client. Light data skills. You can pull numbers from Help Scout or our MCP to back up what you report. An eye for happy customers. You notice them and ask for testimonials and case studies at the right moment. How We Work Together You'll work directly with the founder and with our lead developer. Working with the founder can be intense. Here is what that looks like in practice: Replies are short and can come across as harsh. If something written lands badly or isn't clear, ask. Direction can change. The founder may say one thing, then something different a few days later as they learn more. When that happens, check what changed and adapt. Information should be short and to the point. Lead with what matters, then give more details if asked. The founder can stay frustrated about a problem until it's solved. That's something they are aware of and working on. You'll do well here if you can stay calm and focused when the pressure is on. The team often thinks fast and interrupts each other when discussing ideas. If that would bother you, this role probably isn't for you. This role suits someone with high emotional intelligence, who doesn't take things personally, asks when something is unclear, and keeps many things moving at once. Your schedule can be flexible. If you have a martial arts class every Thursday at 3 pm, go and make up the time later. In return, on the rare occasion the team needs your help on a weekend, we ask you to be flexible too. Benefits Contract type: full-time or part-time Compensation: $2,500 to $4,000 USD per month, depending on experience and location. US-based hires will work as independent contractors (1099). allJobs.description: We are looking for a patient, caring and adaptable Teaching Assistant to provide 1:1 support for a pupil at St Clement’s CE Primary School. You will help the pupil take an active part in classroom learning, build positive relationships and develop confidence and independence. We are a Church of England primary school and part of Aquila, The Diocese of Canterbury Academies Trust. Our Christian vision, “For nothing will be impossible with God” (Luke 1:37), shapes our belief that every child can achieve with the right support. About the role Work with the class teacher and SENCo to put agreed strategies and adjustments into practice. Use practical resources, visual prompts and clear instructions to help the pupil access learning alongside their classmates. Support the pupil through classroom routines and transitions, using a calm and consistent approach. Give the pupil time to try things independently and adjust your support as their confidence grows. Share observations with the class teacher to help identify what is working and what needs to change. We are looking for someone who Builds warm, trusting relationships with children and has high expectations for what they can achieve. Stays calm, flexible and consistent when a child needs extra support. Communicates well and works closely with teachers and other support staff. Understands inclusive practice and is willing to learn and use strategies tailored to the pupil. Experience supporting children with SEND would be welcome. We warmly encourage visits to the school. To arrange a tour or an informal conversation, please contact the school office. We encourage early applications and reserve the right to close this vacancy early if a suitable candidate is found.
